sentences.zh: 宰相者，上承天子，下統百司，治體繫焉。

translations.literal: The chancellor bears up the Son of Heaven above and commands the hundred offices below; upon this the body politic depends.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor bears up the Son of Heaven above and commands the hundred ministries below; the order of government depends on it.

sentences.zh: 元初，將相大臣，年月疏闊，簡牘未詳者則闕之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, for generals and ministers the years and months were sparse; where documents were not detailed, entries are left blank.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuan, dates for generals and ministers were often incomplete; where records are unclear, entries are omitted.

sentences.zh: 中統建元以來，宰執之官，其拜罷歲月之可考者，列而書之。

translations.literal: Since the establishment of the Zhongtong era, for chancellor-offices, those whose appointment and dismissal years and months can be verified are listed and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the Zhongtong era onward, for each chancellor post, appointees and the dates of their appointment and dismissal are listed wherever records allow.

translations.literal: [We] compile the Annals Table of Chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals Table of Chancellors is compiled.
